not_fixed.item: G7: this domain's share of the substep-cost increase (+0.031 ms/substep: ADOPT record 0.059 -> P1 0.090; same-day A/B 0.070 -> 0.104) is not removed by domain code alone
not_fixed.why: Measured: the whole increase is the first build of this domain's nine static indexes through the kernel's M3 read views (World._matching evaluates every predicate inside a step through a _ReadView / _StartView: 2.8 ms per house vs 1.2 ms plain; steady state unchanged, 0.044 vs 0.047 ms over 400 substeps). The kernel's declared-read fast path only applies when the whole step journal and quiet set are empty, which never holds in a system. The exact domain-only alternatives fail: one merged index with derived per-class lists would read the classes' fields on live records, not on step-start records (inexact under the M3 contract), and prebuilding at episode_start only moves the cost out of the bench window. With the kernel request below prototyped (scratch kernel_fastpath.py) and this round's declared reads, the two systems cost 0.070-0.076 ms (ADOPT 0.069-0.071), i.e. the share is removed with no further domain change.

requests.request: house_sim/kernel/world.py World._matching: the declared-read fast path (`if reads is not None and not (journal or quiet)`) never applies inside a step (every system lookup has a non-empty journal; the thermal system's set_quiet writes make hundreds of entities quiet), so every first build and pending re-evaluation of a static index runs a _ReadView / _StartView per entity, about 2.3-3x a plain scan -- this domain's whole G7 share and likely part of every domain's. Change (exact): when reads is declared, evaluate predicate(record) on the plain record for each entity with ('entities', eid) not in self._journal and (eid not in self._quiet or frozenset(reads).isdisjoint(self._quiet[eid])) -- that record IS its step-start record for the fields the predicate reads -- and use the start view only for the rest; keep registering the declared reads as now. Suggest that under STRICT_INDEX the view path stays on for every entity so strict runs keep checking declarations. Drop-in prototype and measurements: scratch p1f_admin_inventory/kernel_fastpath.py; ab_bench.py (admin systems 0.104 -> 0.070-0.076 ms/substep, ADOPT 0.070); index_build2.py (nine admin indexes per house in a step 2.8 -> 1.19 ms); perf_equiv.py (equal digests, normal and strict). World.of_type already declares ('type', 'is_a') and gains everywhere; other domains can declare reads the way admin_inventory.common.reads does.
